CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES
OF THE GOVERNMENT HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
II. Budgetary Allocation
Recommendation/Observation
1.1 The Committee observes that in a resource constrained country like India, the efficient
deployment of the available resources is the key for success of any programe scheme. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should initiate concrete measures for
efficient use of the allocated funds and remove apparent inefficiencies at every level of programme
implementation.
(Para 2.5)
Action Taken
1.2 Annual Action Plan has been drawn, linking Activities to the timelines at State AIDS Control
Society (SACS). This is regularly monitored at periodic interval. Instructions are regularly being
issued to emphasize efficient utilization of funds.
Recommendation/Observation
1.3 The Committee expresses its serious concern that the actual expenditure of the Department
for the year 2010-11 was Rs. 1167.21 crore as against the BE of Rs. 1435.00 crore; for the year
2011-12, Rs. 1313.86 crore as against BE of Rs. 1700.00 crore, and for the year 2012-13,
Rs. 1345.16 crore as against BE of Rs. 1700.00 crore. The Committee expresses its disappointment
at this persistent trend of under-utilization of the budgeted funds and is of the view that this trend
is not only indicative of fiscal indiscipline but also points to slack monitoring of utilization of the
sanctioned provisions. The Committee feels that the reasons adduced by the Department cannot
justify shortfall in expenditure to the tune of Rs. 267.79 crore in 2010-11, Rs. 386.14 crore in
2011-12 and Rs. 354.84 crore in 2012-13. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Department should put in place a strict and effective monitoring mechanism to ensure that the
funds allocated to the Department are monitored quarterly, and exercise utmost fiscal prudence and
discipline so as to make realistic Budget Estimates in future. The Committee desires to be apprised
of the measures initiated in this regard.
(Para 2.9)
Action Taken
1.4 Regular monitoring is being done. Monthly Financial Management letter has been initiated to
keep a track on expenditure, advanced and utilization of funds in the programme.
Recommendation/Observation
1.5 The Committee appreciates that due to the efforts made by the Department, there has been
a considerable decline in unspent balances available with the SACS. The Committee would,
2

3
however, like to point out that availability of unspent balance with some SACS, like Andhra Pradesh
SACS (Rs.23.33 crore), Bihar SACS (Rs.18.23 crore), Gujarat SACS (Rs.14.58 crore), Karnataka
SACS (Rs.26.60 crore) is still quite high. The Committee emphasizes that the Department should
make concerted efforts to get resolved all the unspent balances with the societies so that funds
do not accumulate and remain unutilized. The Committee recommends that in order to ensure timely
and effective utilization of unspent balances, the Department should insist on quarterly feedback
from all the State AIDS Control Societies. Close monitoring of their activities and spending will
certainly deliver the desired results. (Para 2.12)
Action Taken
1.6 Close Monitoring has been initiated and further releases have been linked to cash balances
with SACS. Monthly, unspent balances are being initiated with SACS and instructed to liquidate the
same.
IV. Setting up of new Blood Component Separation Units (BCSUs)
Recommendation/Observation
1.7 The Committee is not aware as to what headway has been made towards concretizing the
above proposal. Considering the fact that blood transfusion is a life-saving treatment in many
situations but it can also be a quick route for the transmission of infectious agents such as HIV ,
HBC, HCV , etc; the Committee recommends that urgent measure be taken on war footing to
regulate Blood Banks. The Committee desires to be furnished with a Status Note, indicating the
initiatives taken by the Department towards ensuring quality management systems and monitoring
of Blood Banks and the outcome thereof.
(Para 4.3)
Action Taken
1.8 Blood banks are under the regulatory control of the State Drug control authorities under the
Drugs and Cosmetics Act. Blood banks cannot function without a licence, which is issued by the
state authorities following approval of the DCGI.
1.9 The efforts of department of AIDS control has taken up the initiative to set up a core
committee in the states with representatives from the state drug control authorities, blood bank
experts and representatives of state AIDS control societies/State blood transfusion councils to
periodically inspect the blood banks to monitor their conformance to existing policy guidelines and
regulations.
1.10  Comprehensive standards to ensure better quality control system on collection, storage,
testing and distribution of blood and its components have been formulated and disseminated.

resumed in the other States also in the current financial year.
XIII. HIV/AIDS Bill
Recommendation/Observation
3.27 The Committee observes that much delay has already taken place in introducing the AIDS
Bill in Parliament. The Committee recommends that the Department should proactively pursue the
matter for getting the Bill vetted from the Ministry of Law and Justice without any further any
delay so that the Bill may be introduced in the Parliament at the earliest. The Committee does not
understand the reasons why it should take more than ten years to finalise a Bill when a decision
was taken in 2002. The Bill is yet to be finalized. The delay is not justifiable when the problem
is enormous and India is third largest AIDS/HIV affected Country.
(Para 13.3)
Action Taken
3.28 The Department of AIDS Control is closely working with the Ministry of Law & Justice
to finalize the HIV/AIDS (Prevention & Control) Bill 2013. A Draft Note for Cabinet in this regard
has been prepared by the Department of AIDS Control and sent to the Ministry of Law & Justice
on 6.6.2013. On behalf of the Ministry of Law & Justice, the Dept. of Legal Affairs is to submit
its opinion and the Legislative Department is to vet the Draft Bill. This is currently under process
and once these steps have been completed the same will be sent for approval of the Cabinet.
Department of AIDS Control is ensuring that all due procedures are followed prior to tabling of
the Bill in Parliament.
Further Recommendation
3.29 The Committee feels that inspite of numerous recommendations made by it, the said
Bill seems to be stuck up for reasons best known to the Ministry. The Committee would
like the Ministry to take its recommendations with the seriousness it deserves and
recommends that the Secretary of the Department of AIDS Control should personally
monitor the progress of the Bill to ensure its introduction in the Parliament at the earliest.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS — AT A GLANCE
II. Budgetary Allocation
The Committee is not satisfied with the lackadaisical approach of the Department in
the matter. It has been more than one and a half years since 12 th Plan Period started,
however, the Department could submit NACP-IV project in July, 2013 for CCEA approval.
The Committee observes that delay in this regard may undermine the desired outcome in
the NACP-IV project. The Committee would like the Department to take pro-active action
in this matter and take all possible measures to check any further delay. (Para 3.3)
III. Role of NGOs.
The Committee takes note of the initiatives taken by the Department for recovering
the balance amount from the remaining States. However, the Committee observes that no
tangible steps have been taken or contemplated to be taken to accomplish the task. The
Committee would like the Department to indicate a specific action plan to sort out the
glitches with NGOs for achieving the targets and also put in place some tangible guidelines
on basis of which the NGOs would be identified in future. (Para 3.7)
IV. Setting up of new Blood Component Separation Units (BCSUs)
The Committee finds it hard to come to the view that the matter of setting up the
four metro Blood Banks has come to a naught since it was first initiated in 2009. The
Committee feels that the Department has not been able to convince the EFC in plausible
terms the financial as well as the social viability of the setting up of the Blood Banks. The
Committee would like to be apprised of the observations made by the Department of
Expenditure, Ministry of Finance in the revised proposal for the Blood Banks for
consideration by the EFC. The Committee would also like to be apprised of the progress
made in acquisition of land in respect of all the four blood banks. (Para 3.18)
V. Setting up of new District level Blood Banks
The Committee is not satisfied with languid pace of the progress made for setting up
of 11 DLBB out of 39 DLBB which was a target of Phase-III of NACP. Most of the reasons
cited in this regard seem purely procedural. The Committee would like the Department to
sort out the hurdles in this regard so that appropriate result can come out. The Department
should also consider providing appropriate additional funds, if required, for infrastructure
and manpower related matters so that there is no delay due to financial constraints.
(Para 3.23)
IX. Adolescence Education Programme (AEP)
The Committee while appreciating the efforts made by the Department in resuming
AEP in Karnataka, would like to impress upon the Department to ensure that AEP is
resumed in the other States also in the current financial year. (Para 3.26)

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES
OF THE GOVERNMENT HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
II. Budgetary Allocation
Recommendation/Observation
1.1 The Committee observes that the five new schemes/projects of the Department of Health
Research could not be made operational even during 2012-13 due to lack of approvals, though the
Department had come into existence in 2007 and become functional in 2008 with the appointment
of its first Secretary. The Committee is unable to comprehend the reasons for not getting the
required approvals even after a lapse of five years since the creation of the Department, which has
resulted in massive financial under-performance vis-à-vis the approved outlay of Rs. 4496.08 crore
for the Eleventh Plan. The Committee has been exhorting the Department to pay focused attention
for completing all pre-project formalities and obtaining necessary approvals on time so that the
budgeted funds are not locked up for want of approvals and surrendered later. The Committee is,
however, constrained to note that little attention seems to have been paid to its advice in this regard
which has resulted in persistent and substantial under-utilisation of budgeted funds. The first year
of the Twelfth Plan Period has already lapsed and the current year is the 2
nd year of the Twelfth
Plan. The Committee notes that the EFC approval for the three new Schemes were accorded, albeit

II. Budgetary Allocation
Recommendation/Observation
2.1 The Committee notes that there is significant variation between the Budget Estimates and
the actual expenditure incurred in respect of the five new schemes of the Department. Persistent
mismatch between the Budget Estimates and the actual expenditure indicates that budget
formulation is being done without applying proper financial yardsticks. The Committee feels that
there is an imperative need to minimize the huge mismatch between the Budget Estimates and the
actual expenditure so as to observe the fiscal norms in letter and spirit. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that corrective measures be initiated and implemented for realistic projection of fund
requirements of the Department in future.
(Para 2.7)
Action Taken
2.2 The provisions of General Financial Rules and the guidelines issued by the Ministry of
Finance (Budget Division) for budget formulation, financial management and periodical
monitoring are duly followed by the Department of Health Research. Since all the schemes
formulated by DHR are new schemes to fulfil the objectives as per the mandate of the newly
created department, budget provisions for these schemes are being made from time to time
based on the total estimated project cost as well as the year-wise phasing of physical and
financial targets of the schemes. It is necessary to make requisite budgetary provisions for the
schemes as in the absence of this, the schemes are not taken up for consideration and
appraisal. However, despite best efforts by the Department, the schemes could not be approved
during the Eleventh Plan.
2.3 Now since the three schemes have already been approved and sanctioned and the
remaining two schemes are also expected to be cleared during the current financial year,
maximum utilization of budgeted funds is expected with the implementation of the schemes. The
suggestion of the Committee for making realistic projection of fund requirements is noted for
compliance.
Recommendation/Observation
2.4 The Committee observes that the ICMR is the main technical wing of the Department of
Health Research and is responsible for formulation, coordination and promotion of bio-medical
research in the country. The Committee, therefore, notes with serious concern the likely adverse
impact of the funds crunch on the intramural and extramural research priorities of ICMR. The
Committee desires that Planning Commission/Ministry of Finance may reconsider the allocation for
ICMR for the Twelfth Plan after making a fair assessment.
(Para 2.13)

II. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
Recommendation/Observation
3.1 The Committee observes that scientific knowledge generated through health and bio-medical
research is used to develop drugs, diagnostics, vaccines and devices that ultimately find place in
the health care systems of the country. It is also worth mentioning that health research has a vital
role to play in the discovery and development of indigenous health products. Taking all these
factors into account, the Committee apprehends that allowing the new schemes to be plagued with
under-funding from the very beginning would prove detrimental to generation of new knowledge
in the area of health research. The Committee, therefore, lends its support for enhancement of
funds for the schemes at the RE stage. The Committee, simultaneously, recommends to the
Department to pay focused attention to more efficient deployment of the available resources.
(Para 2.10)
Action Taken
3.2 The Department of Health Research appreciates the support from the Honourable Members
of the Parliamentary Standing Committee for recommending enhancement of the budgetary
allocation of the Department at the RE stage for its various schemes. The Department will put
forward the recommendations of the Committee to the Planning Commission/ Ministry of Finance
while discussing the Revised Estimate for additional allocation of budget.
3.3 The Department will pay special attention and take care towards efficient deployment of
available resources.
Further Recommendations
3.4 While making its recommendation in para 2.10 of its 69
th Report, the Committee had
expected the Department to formulate effective measures for efficient deployment of
available resources. Merely stating that the “Department will pay special attention and take
care towards efficient deployment of available resources”, is not sufficient. The Committee
would, therefore, recommend to the Department to formulate and implement measures for
more productive use of the available resources. The Committee would like to be apprised
of the steps taken in this regard.

VI. Grant–in–Aid Schemes for Inter-Sectoral Convergence & Promotion and Guidance
on Research Governance Issues
Recommendation/Observation
3.14 The Committee recommends that early action be taken for setting up MTDB which will go
a long way in promoting development of indigenous medical technologies.
(Para 6.9)
Action Taken
3.15 Action is already underway to establish proposed Medical Technology Assessment Board
(MTAB) in the Department of Health Research, which primarily aims to assess/evaluate the
appropriateness and cost-effectiveness and essentiality of the available and new health technologies
in India. Department will like to apprise the committee that this Board will be an authority for
extracting available evidence and gather other data/information through model projects for
improving the research governance in health in India.
● The MTAB would examine the numerous and heterogeneous health technology
providers, payers and adopters in India.
● The MTAB would be empowered to make recommendations to the Government of
India after suitable health technology assessment systems through evaluation on the
appropriateness and cost effectiveness of medical technologies, interventions and
procedures for introduction/procurement in India.
● The MTAB would be set up through consultation with stake holders like technology
generators, industry, regulators, economists, user groups and experts knowledgeable
about similar medical/health technology assessment systems abroad like NICE, UK and
similar models from Canada, Australia, Thailand etc.
● The MTAB will be a part of the overall regulatory/promotional structure being
established in the DHR to accelerate indigenous production of health products/
instruments/medical devices that are vital for providing cost effective health care.
● As part of this initiative, a MOU has just been signed between the DHR and the
National Institute of Clinical Excellence (NICE), UK. Follow-up action is being initiated
to identify areas for collaboration for exchange of knowledge on procedures used by
NICE for regulatory arrangements in UK in the first phase.

X. Manpower Requirements of Department of Health Research
Recommendation/Observation
4.3 The Committee notes that despite coming into existence of DHR as a separate Department
in 2007, the cadre-controlling authority for the DHR is the Department of Health and Family
Welfare. The purpose being served by having such an arrangement is beyond the comprehension
of the Committee. The Committee feels that such an arrangement would only delay the process of
filling up of vacant posts and should, therefore, be dispensed with. The Committee would
therefore, like the Department of Health Research to bring the above observation to the notice of
the authorities concerned for an appropriate decision. The Committee desires to be apprised of the
response of Department of Health and Family Welfare in this regard.
(Para 10.3)
Action Taken
4.4 The Department appreciates the recommendations of the Committee that cadre controlling
of DHR should not be Department of Health and Family Welfare. Department of Health is the cadre
controlling authority in respect of Secretarial Services viz. CSS/CSSS/CSCS. As the Department
has only limited posts of these services having a separate cadre may not be feasible. However, the
Department will explore possibilities with the concerned authorities for appropriate action in this
matter to fill up the post on urgent basis. The Observation of Committee will be communicated
and the Committee will be apprised of the response.

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES
OF THE GOVERNMENT HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
II. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
Recommendation/Observation
1.1 From a glance of the above Table, the Committee notes that the funds allocated over the
period of Eleventh Plan and Annual Plan 2012-13 has increased steadily. However, the Committee
is constrained to observe that in a time of increasing demand due to demographic pressures, public
expectations and medical advances there was substantial and persistent under-utilization of the
budgeted funds during the Eleventh Plan and Annual Plan of 2012-13. The Committee desires that
the processes of allocation and utilization of funds should be mutually reinforcing instead of being
parallel. That the savings occurred under the Plan head underlines the fact that the development
activities might have been adversely affected in the health sector. The Committee, accordingly
impresses upon the Department that in future utilization must reflect the allocation policy objectives
to the extent possible. (Para 2.2)
Action Taken
1.2 Noted for compliance.
Recommendation/Observation
1.3 The Committee’s examination of the following major heads of account as per the
background material furnished by the Department has revealed recurrent and persistent sub-optimal
utilization of budgetary provisions (Plan) during the last three Financial years (Annexure-A).
Actual expenditure incurred in respect of some of the major Institutions/projects/initiatives
of Department for the last three financial years is as under Annexure-B. (Para 2.7)
Action Taken
1.4 Matter of Record.
Recommendation/Observation
1.5 From a perusal of the above Tables, the Committee observes that with such level of
underutilization of funds, the financial objectives and target achievement of the Department would
suffer to a large extent. The Department has informed that during the Eleventh Plan the extent of
savings on the Capital Account has been Rs.2883.25 crore. Most of the savings were due to slow
progress of capital work and slow pace of procurement of equipments. The Committee observes
with deep concern that savings under the Capital section implies that it will impede the
2

3
developmental activities. Slow progress in capital work would critically hamper both the quality of
care provided and the ability of the system as a whole to respond to increased demand in this
sector. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should take concrete steps to
address this issue by means of prudent assessment of the fund requirement and design effective
mechanism to make a balance between spending and savings. (Para 2.8)

Recommendations/Observations

for settlement of Medical Reimbursement Claims (MRC) and that a report of the MRCs pending

documents from the beneficiary and also opinion from specialists of Government hospitals.
However, Instructions have been issued to settle the Medical Reimbursement Claims within the
shortest possible time. A maximum time-limit of 45 days has been fixed for this purpose within

the Government is making efforts to address this problem. CGHS, like other Government

institutions is also facing the shortage of doctors. So far as fresh recruitments are concerned UPSC

of promotional posts. However, many of the selected candidates against direct recruitment do not
join CGHS. Retired doctors have been hired on contract basis against some of the vacant posts
to manage the operations depending on the immediate need. The existing CGHS Wellness Centres
and other formations are working in efficient manner with the human resources available at present.
However, the point made by the Hon’ble Committee is noted and the Department shall make further
efforts to fill up the vacancies and strengthen the human resources wherever required to improve
the functioning of CGHS.
Recommendations/Observations
1.22 The Committee was apprised that timings of CGHS dispensaries have been revised so as
to provide extended hours of the Wellness Centres. The Department has informed that to overcome
the problem of shortage of doctors and paramedical staff and ensure optimum utilization of scarce
manpower resources, it was decided to change the working hours of the CGHS dispensaries from
the current timings of 7.30 AM to 1.30 PM to 8.00 AM to 3.00 PM with 30 minutes of lunch
break. The new timings have been implemented in Delhi NCR with effect from 1st April, 2013.

computerization of all CGHS dispensaries and universal application and portability of CGHS cards,

1.26 On the query of the Committee on the steps being taken to ensure that the instructions
issued to the CMO in charge of all the Wellness Centres to stop the pilferage of medicines is being
scrupulously followed, the Department informed that CMOs in-Charge are expected to adhere to
the detailed instructions issued to them in this regard. To ensure that the instructions are followed
by them properly, the following steps have been taken:
(a) The CMOs In-charge are sensitized about it regularly by the Additional Director of the
concerned zone/ city in the monthly meetings.
(b) Surprise Inspections are carried out by the superior officers to verify the stock of
drugs/medicines in the dispensary stores /counters.
(c) Internal Audit Unit of Vigilance Division of CGHS does surprise visits to know as to
whether the guidelines to stop pilferage of medicines are being adhered to.
(d) Appropriate actions are taken in case of non-compliance of the instructions.
(e) To exercise an effective check on pilferage of medicines from the CGHS Wellness
centres, an ‘SMS Alert system’ has been introduced. A system generated message is
sent to the CGHS beneficiaries indicating that he/she has been issued medicines from
the CGHS dispensary. Registration of Mobile number has also been made compulsory.
(Para 3.13)
1.27 In this regard the Committee recommends that in addition to the steps already taken by the
Department, it should also be ensured that there is no leakage at the transit stage. Comparable

1.28 The following measures have been taken to ensure quality of medicines supplied to CGHS
and to prevent pilferage of CGHS medicines;

Pilot Project, in-house analysis report of the drugs is submitted by the Manufacturer/
Distributor. As far as procurement through HSCC is concerned, a joint team of HSCC
and CGHS draws random 2
nd samples from the supplied drugs under inspection and

testing.
2. Same procedure is followed for Pilot project drugs, except for the samples for
2
nd analysis are drawn by the CMO In-charges.

measures are taken by state Drug Control Department.

transparency and accountability;
● Proper maintenance of stock records.
● Stock position/availability of medicines can be viewed online by the CMO I/Cs for
proper utilisation of medicines.
● Short supplies/over supplies of medicines are looked into immediately for taking
remedial measures.

Recommendation/Observation
1.45 As per the information furnished by the Department Rs.476.00 crore and Rs.788.70 Crore
has been allocated under Plan and Non-Plan respectively for the financial year 2012-13. Out of
Plan allocation, Rs.247.24 crore has been expended till February, 2013. However, as per the
information furnished by the Department vide its OM dated 4
th April, 2013 the utilization till
March 31, 2013 was Rs. 470.00 crore. The Committee fails to understand as to how a huge
amount was expended in the last month of the financial year. The Department needs to explain
this. However, the Committee observes that the allocation under Non-Plan has been fully utilized.
(Para 9.2)

12
Action Taken
1.46 Out of the allocation Rs.476 crore, grant released to the Institute was Rs. 470 crore only
under Plan for the year 2012-13. Expenditure incurred till March 31, 2013 was Rs.423.13 crore,
out of which Rs.247. 24 crore was expended till Feb.2013. Expenditure of Rs.175.89 crore under
Plan during the month of March is because of various stages involved in procurement process and
execution of capital projects, which are specified hereunder;
The requirement of Machinery and Equipment of each Centre/Department in AIIMS is
assessed by Assessment Committee in the beginning of the financial year. On the basis of detailed
presentation made by Heads of Departments/Chief of Centres before the Assessment Committee
chaired by Director, allocation of funds is made. This exercise is generally completed by Ist week
of May.
The Institute faculty has summer vacation in two groups from 16
th May-15 June and the
16th June-15 th July. The majority of the technical specifications are made available to the Store
section only during August when all the faculty joins after availing the summer vacation. For the
equipments where the threshold value is more than Rs.30 lakh, external experts are also associated
in preparation of specifications and these are made available to the store section for floating the
tender by mid-September.
The institute floats about 700-800 tenders for different equipments. Wide publicity of
tenders is given and tender submission requires about 1-1/2 month’s time. Thereafter, the analysis
of bids is carried out. Technical evaluation including demonstration of the equipments, wherever
required, also takes about 1-1/2 month’s time. Then, the Store Purchase Committee meetings, Price
Bid Opening meetings, Negotiations Meetings are held and also concurrence of Finance Division
and approval of Competent Authority is obtained before award of contracts, which takes another
about 2-3 months time.
In some cases, re-tendering has to be done due to single bid or single shortlisted bid with
a view to generate more competition for which specifications are also sometimes re-visited and
made more broad based. Thus, majority of contracts are finalized during the last quarter only.
In case of indigenous equipments or imported equipments offered in Indian Rupees,
generally a lead time of 1-2 months is to be given to suppliers to supply the stores and accordingly
the supplies are received in the months of February-March. After the receipt of supplies and
issuance of Inspection Notes, the payments are released.
In case of imported equipments in foreign currency, the letters of credit is established
through the State Bank of India Foreign Exchange Division and they also require some processing
time. Majority of the letters of credit are opened in the month of March only.
Expenditure on capital works is generally made on circumstantial need in line with the
project/work status. Payments made were against works already completed and for works which
were taken up at the end of 2012-13.

Recommendation/Observation
1.65 The C ommittee takes a serious view of the fake, substandard, spurious and adulterated
medicines being detected in such large number of cases. This amounts to playing with the lives of
the people. This can not be tolerated. All the States should be asked to prosecute all the cases. The
CDSCO may regularly review the progress and apprise the Committee. The Committee recommends
that research should be undertaken for synthesizing international experience on the key issues and
technology advancement. The Committee also recommends that Standard Operating Procedures
(SOPs) for approval of new drugs and clinical trials should be expedited. (Para 16.10)
Action Taken
1.66 A survey to assess the extent of spurious drugs in the country was conducted in the
year 2009 by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO). The survey was
statistically designed by the Indian Statistical Institute, Hyderabad. Under the study, 24,136 samples
of 62 brands of drugs were drawn from different outlets spread over the country. The survey
revealed that the extent of drugs found spurious was 0.046% only. Further, as per the information
made available by the State Drugs Controllers in respect of the drugs samples tested during
last three years, the percentage of substandard drugs varied from 5.70% in 2008-09 to 4.54% in
2011-12.
1.67 Notwithstanding these figures, the Government has taken the following measures to check
Spurious/Sub-standard Drugs in the country:
1. The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 was amended by the Drugs and Cosmetics
(Amendment) Act, 2008 to provide for more stringent penalties for manufacture and
trade of spurious and adulterated drugs. Certain offences have also been made
cognizable and non-bailable. 
2. The Drugs and Cosmetics (Amendment) Act, 2008 has also enabled setting up of
special designated courts for speedy disposal of cases to deal with the cases of
offences under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. 16 States/UTs have already set up these
special Courts. 

19
3. Guidelines for taking action on samples of drugs declared spurious or not of standard
quality in the light of enhanced penalties under the Drugs and Cosmetics (Amendment)
Act, 2008 have been forwarded to the State Drugs Controllers for implementation. 
4. A Whistle Blower Scheme has been initiated by the Government to encourage vigilant
public participation in the detection of movement of spurious drugs in the country.
Under this scheme, the informers would be suitably rewarded for providing concrete
information in respect of movement of spurious drugs to the regulatory authorities. 
5. On the basis of an Order of the Hon’ble High Court of Allahabad in the Criminal
(Misc.) Writ Petition No. 16212/2008 – Brahmaji vs. State of UP and Others, the
Government had constituted a Task Force to examine the feasibility of networking and
tracking the drugs distribution system in the country from the manufacturer to the
retailer to secure the entire supply chain and detect spurious drugs available in the
market. Different options through the use of information technology were considered
by the Task Force, including providing bar code on the label of the drugs, for
identifying and tracking their movement from the manufacturer to the consumer. On
the basis of the recommendations of the Task Force and further consultation with the
stakeholders, the Government conducted a study with the help of the National
Informatics Centre to examine the feasibility of networking and tracking the drugs
distribution system in the country from the manufacturer to the retailer by the use of
modern information technological tools to detect spurious drugs available in the market.
6. Overseas inspections of drug manufacturing sites to ensure quality of imported bulk
drugs were started in 2011.
7. 216 additional posts were created in 2008 and 2009 for strengthening CDSCO
headquarters and ports/zonal offices. It has further, been proposed to create 1045
additional posts in the CDSCO on regular basis to strengthen it. The proposal has been
recommended by the Working Group on Drug Sector, constituted by the Planning
Commission in 12th Five Year Plan under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Ministry of
Health and Family Welfare. In the first phase, a proposal for creation of 365 posts in
CDSCO has already been sent to the Department of Expenditure.  The labs also
similarly need strengthening. A proposal for creation of 283 posts in labs has also been
sent to the Department of Expenditure. The 283 posts do not include additional posts
for Central Drugs Laboratories at Kolkata and Kasauli as their organisational structure
need to be evaluated. There may be the need for around 60 additional personnel for
these two labs. The CDSCO and labs need strengthening and upgradation of their
physical infrastructure also. The labs need new and sophisticated equipments. Several
new labs need to be opened. Similarly existing zonal/sub-zonal/port/airport offices of
CDSCO need upgradation of their physical infrastructure. The such offices also need
to be opened. The CDSCO also need to open its offices abroad to monitor imports.
All these areas are proposed to be covered during the 12th Five Year Plan for which
the CDSCO has been allocated Rs.1800 crore.
During the Twelfth Five Year Plan, a provision of Rs.1200 crore has also been made for
strengthening of the drug regulatory system of the states.

Recommendation/Observation

to convince the Ministry of Finance/Planning Commission, it needs to put in place a strong and
effective physically and financially prudent system which is able to absorb the funds allocated to
it, which does not seem to be the case now in view of the persistent underutilization of the funds
allocated to it year after year under NRHM. The Committee recommends that the Department’s
vision to undertake Universal Health Coverage should not suffer due to non-allocation of funds for
NUMH and dropping of implementation thereof. The Committee is very much concerned with the
sorry state of affairs of healthcare facilities presently available to urban poor particularly those
living in urban slums. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should make all
out efforts to get more funds at RE stage for implementation of some of the schemes under
NUHM. Besides, the funds meant for NRHM should not be directed for NUHM. (Para 2.8)
Action Taken
1.2 The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for compliance. It is informed that
the Finance Minister, vide letter dated 13
th May, 2013, has informed that funds would be made
available for NUHM. Internally also efforts are being made to mobilize resource towards NUHM.
Recommendation/Observation
1.3 The Committee feels that the total Expenditure by Government (Central and State
Governments combined) as a percentage of GDP has merely increased from 1.27 in 2007-08 to
1.29 in 2011-12 which is a very telling comment on the state of affairs of public spending on
Health which directly translates into high Out-of-Pocket expenses for a majority of population. The
Committee observes that given the fact that a significant percent of India’s population is
impoverished every year due to illness of a family member, there is an imperative need to increase
the total expenditure at the Centre and the States level to at least 3% of GDP. Since the States
are themselves under fiscal stress, it is for the Centre to assign a significant part of its resources
towards health care. The Committee hopes that the Department would be able to live up to the
contention of the Planning Commission for increasing the total Government expenditure, both at
centre and state level as a proportion of GDP in the Twelfth Plan from 1.94 percent in the last
year of the Eleventh Plan to 3.04 percent in the corresponding year of the twelfth Plan given the
dismal utilization figures of the Department in the Eleventh Plan. (Para 2.13)

51

1. Introduction of case based web based system of electronic recording and reporting of TB

developed Case based web based system of electronic recording and reporting of TB
cases (Nikshay) which was launched on 15th May, 2013 after quick testing of

Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme. Till now, we have 1.2 million cases
entered in this application. This ensures appropriate and effective treatment of all TB
cases to prevent drug resistant TB. This application also includes details of Multi-Drug
Resistant (MDR) patients and HIV associated Tuberculosis. Auto generation of
Programme reports and epidemiological analysis is also being done.

suspect criteria to include all re-treatment smear positive TB cases.

detected compared to the sputum smear microscopy across the 18 sites across
12 states.

● Provider Initiated HIV Testing and Counselling (PITC) among Presumptive TB cases
(TB suspects) is now a policy which is being implemented on priority in High HIV
prevalent states/settings. In low HIV prevalent states/settings – HIV testing among
presumptive TB cases should be routinely implemented in the age-group of 25-54 years

● A state-wide representative sample of TB patients in Kerala was conducted. Wherein

Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS) is being implemented.

patients will also be extended to those districts.

CHAPTER-III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES
OF THE GOVERNMENT HA VE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
II. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
Recommendation/Observation
3.1 Approved outlay for National Health Mission (NHM) for the Twelfth Plan is Rs.193405.71
crores as against the projected outlay of Rs.219702.45 crores. Further against a projected demand
for Rs.32,520.13 crore for NHM, the Planning Commission has approved an outlay of Rs.20999.00
crore for 2013-14. The Committee is aware that public spending on health was targeted to be
increased to 2.5% of GDP at the launch of NRHM in 2005. However, as per figures quoted by
the Economic Survey 2012-13, public expenditure on health is just 1.29% of GDP. Private
expenditure on health is 2.9% of GDP. The Committee observes that even if the level of
government expenditure on health is increased to 2.5% of GDP, there would still be a very
substantial health care expenditure which is out-of-pocket payments made by the households in
time of health distress. The cost of health care services in the private sector is so exorbitant that
it is just unaffordable for the poor and the under-privileged. It is in this context that the reduction
in approved outlay of Rs.193405.71 crore for NHM for the Twelfth Plan against the projected
demand of Rs.219702.45 crore is cause for extreme concern to the Committee. Keeping in view
the fact that illness of a family member is the most common reason leading to a financial crisis
among poor households, the Committee lends its full support for greater health outlays. The
Committee, simultaneously, recommends that the Department should strengthen its monitoring
mechanism so as to ensure that the available resources are utilized more efficiently and
responsibility be fixed to ensure timely disbursement and utilization of funds at all levels.
(Para 2.2)
Action Taken
3.2 The Ministry is in agreement with the views of the Committee. There is need to enhance
the outlay for the Health sector to reduce the out of pocket expenditure burden, particularly for
the poor and unprivileged sections of the society. The Ministry is also undertaking necessary
measures to monitor and improve the efficiency of available resources and also monitor timely
disbursement of funds at all levels through CPSMS, etc.
Further Recommendation
3.3 The Committee feels that mere agreement with its views would not suffice. The
Committee would like to be informed of the steps taken so far/contemplated to be taken
in the future to reduce the out-of-pocket payments made by households in time of health
distress. The specific role which the National Health Mission would play in reducing the
exorbitant out-of-pocket expenses, may also be indicated.
Recommendation/Observation
3.4 The Committee is not able to comprehend as to how Department with the approved outlay
71

72
of Rs.20999.00 crores for NHM which is just a shade above the Rs.20542.00 crores which the
Department was allocated in 2012-13 for NRHM, would be able to meet the objective of universal
health coverage. The Committee feels that the Department of Health and Family Welfare has not
been able to plausibly convince the Ministry of Finance/ Planning Commission to release the funds
sought by it. The Committee is not aware of the reasons adduced by the Planning Commission for
marginal increase in allocation of funds in BE 2013-14 over BE 2012-13 and would, therefore, like
to be apprised of the same. Further, from the table given above, the Committee gathers that no
funds have been allocated to “Assistance to States for Capacity Building(Burns)’ and Central Drug
Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow’ and a mere Rs.1.00 Crore have been allocated for
“Strengthening of District Hospitals for providing advanced secondary care’; “Providing Free
Generic Medicines in all Public Health Institutions in the country’ and “National Urban Health
Mission-Flexible Pool’. The Committee would like to be apprised of the reasons for such nil/low
allocations in respect of such important Institutes/ Schemes which have a vital bearing on the
progress towards Universal Health Coverage that the Department is aiming to achieve in the near
future . (Para 2.6)
Action Taken
3.5 The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare had proposed Rs.32,520.13 crore as an outlay
for the Financial year 2013-14, whereas the planning commission approved an outlay of
Rs.20,999 crore only. The Ministry made a strong case for higher allocation. The approved 12
th
Plan mentions 322% increase in the twelfth plan outlay to Rs.2,68,551 crore for the Department
of Health and Family Welfare. However, with an annual provision of Rs.20999 crore only, it is not
possible to meet the goal of UHC. The Department will take appropriate action for seeking
enhanced allocation at RE stage.
3.6 For the schemes/activities such as “Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow”,
“No funds have been released to CDRI, Lucknow, as research activities being undertaken by CDRI,
Lucknow have been transferred to Department of Health Research (ICMR) and these are to be
monitored and funded with their own budget”. The National Programme for Prevention and
Management of Burn Injuries has been taken up under the NCD pool under NHM.
3.7 As regards “Providing Free Generic Medicines in all Public Health Institutions in the
country”, ‘Strengthening of District Hospitals for providing advanced secondary care and “National
Urban Health Mission-Flexible Pool”, these schemes were included in the Department’s budget as

true that these Schemes have a vital bearing on the progress towards Universal Health Coverage
that the Department is aiming to achieve.
3.8 However, due to inadequate budgetary allocation at BE stage of 2013-14, which is
effectively lower than the BE of 2012-13 if we exclude the new component of NCD pool in the
NHM, only a token provision could be made but with the hope that if additional resources become
available to the Department at the RE stage or if savings are possible in other approved schemes/
programmes, the budgetary provision for these schemes would be enhanced during the course of
the year.
Further Recommendation
3.9 The Committee is concerned to note that adequate budgetary allocation for schemes
which have a vital bearing on Universal Health coverage, could not be allocated despite the
Ministry’s own admission that these programme were considered important and are
mentioned in the Twelfth Plan Document. The Committee is not aware of the reasons
adduced by Ministry of Finance/Planning Commission for not allocating the required funds

73
and would therefore like to be apprised of the reasons. The Committee also notes that by
now the RE must have been made. The Committee, therefore, desires to be updated
whether the enhanced allocations have been made under this head, and if not, what
alternate arrangements have been made by the Ministry to ensure that the activities
proposed under this head do not suffer due to paucity of funds.
Recommendation/Observation
3.10 The Committee feels that the Department should set a time frame within which the Action
Taken on the findings of the review of NRHM is completed, so as to ensure that the newly
introduced NHM schemes, which includes NRHM as its sub-component, should not suffer due to
the vital gaps in physical infrastructure and Human Resources which have been the bane of proper
implementation of NRHM in the first phase. Government should concentrate on filling up the gaps
particularly the gaps in terms of “Specialist’ and “Nurse’ vacancies in many States particularly in
remote, difficult and tribal areas as noticed in the review of NRHM phase-I. Unless these gaps are
filled up, implementation of the ambitious scheme under NRHM will not yield desired results.
(Para 2.10)
Action Taken
3.11 It is true that ensuring availability of infrastructure and human resources, particularly in
rural areas, is critical to achieving desired health outcomes and is thus one of the key concerns
of NRHM. The Department is systematically trying to address these concerns.
3.12 On the one hand, efforts are being made to increase the number of new institutions and
enhancing the capacity of existing institutions to produce more doctors, nurses and paramedical
staff. Thus, norms have been rationalised in medical education, such as relaxation in land
requirements, bed strength, and increase in ceiling for maximum intake for undergraduates,
enhancement of teacher-student ratio in PG etc. which has resulted in substantial increase in
number of undergraduate and post graduate seats.
3.13 There is also a proposal in the Twelfth Plan to support establishment of new medical
colleges in deficient states and strengthening of Government Medical colleges to increase the MBBS
seats. Government has also approved setting up of ANM/GNM Schools in different States besides
setting up of Institutes of Paramedical Sciences at national and regional levels.
3.14 On the other hand, financial support is provided to States under National Rural Health
Mission (NRHM) for engagement of doctors, specialist and paramedics on contractual basis.
Monetary incentives such as hard areas allowances and special packages are provided to staff in
difficult and most difficult areas. Non-Monetary incentives such as preferential admission in post
graduate courses for staff serving in difficult areas and improving accommodation arrangement in
rural areas have also been introduced. Further, support is also provided under NRHM for multi-
skilling of doctors to overcome the shortage of specialists.
3.15 However, higher resource allocation for NHM is critical to addressing the vital gaps in
physical infrastructure and Human Resources.
Further Recommendation
3.16 The Committee lends its full support to the Ministry’s demand for higher resource
allocation for NHM and recommends that the Planning Commission may be apprised of the
Committee’s view in the matter. The Committee also recommends that the Department of
Health and Family Welfare needs to put its case more effectively before the Planning

Commission/Finance Ministry so as to ensure that more funds are released for NHM. The

XI. MILLENIUM DEVELOPMENT GOALS (MDGS)
Recommendation/Observation
3.56 The Committee feels that the success rate of achievements with regard to Millennium
Development Goals has been a mixed bag of success. While the department is more or less on
track with respect to MDG-4 and MDG-5, the success rate in respect of MDG-6 seems a distant
dream especially with regard to the viral diseases like Dengue, Chikungunya which is a constant
cause of worry year after year, not to mention new diseases like H1N1 which have now started
spreading across the country. The Department should, therefore, put in place a ‘Dedicated Sentinel
Force’ whose main protocol would be ensuring prevention of entry of diseases from outside the
borders(land, sea, air) of the country. Additionally, the Committee feels that the Department should
explore the possibility of tapping the additional resources for mopping up additional funds for its
various programmes particularly for the welfare of our poverty ridden masses. (Para 11.5)
Action Taken
3.57 W ith regard to placing ‘Dedicated Sentinel Force’ in respect of vector borne diseases i.e.
Malaria, Dengue and Chikungunya, it is submitted that Malaria is endemic in all the areas of the
country except areas located above 5000 ft. from the sea level. There is routine surveillance system
to monitor the diseases status in the country. Dengue is also endemic in major part of the country
and Chikungunya has re-emerged and is being reported since 2006. To monitor the situation in the
country 347 sentinel sites have been established in the country.
3.58 A well organized programme called National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme is
being implemented throughout the country for control of vector borne diseases including Malaria,
Dengue and Chikungunya with adequate resource provisions under NRHM. At the state level, there
is a state programme officer for vector borne diseases and at district level, the district malaria
officer now renamed as district VBD officer does exist. District level officers are supported with
technical staff to perform the activities. The programme is integrated under primary health care
system at PHC level.
3.59 The achievements with respect of Millennium Development Goal are as under:
Malaria:
● Millennium Development Goals (MDG) for Malaria  is to halt and begin to reverse the
incidence of malaria and other major diseases by 2015.
● Prevalence and death rates associated with Malaria.
● Proportion population in Malaria risk areas using effective Malaria prevention and
treatment measures (Percentage of population covered under Indoor Residual Spray
(IRS)).

for last one decade. The malaria cases were brought down from 2,031,790 cases in
2000 to 1,816,569 cases in 2005 and further brought down to 1,066,972 cases in
2012. Country is heading towards achieving target of 50% reduction in incidence of
malaria cases against the baseline.

which has come down to 0.04 deaths per lakh population in 2012 as per

Dengue:

XII. IMPLEMENTATION OF NRHM (PHASE-I)
3.63 The Department has delineated the following issues during the implementation of NRHM
(Phase-I):
Problem Areas :
State Government:-
● Low capacities to manage large programmes especially in Empowered Action Group
(EAG) States. The contribution of block level and district level planning structure and
PRI in the planning process was inadequate.
● Inadequate capacities across many States to carry out infrastructure planning and
implementation e.g. lack of dedicated/exclusive civil construction wing especially under
NRHM and lack of systems with regards to external evaluation and monitoring of
construction works taken up across States.
● Non-availability and uneven distribution of skilled health care provider including critical
manpower like specialists, nurses etc. especially in EAG States is a challenge. High

84
attrition rates of HR, due to lack of clear cut HR Policies and inadequate career
progression opportunities. Deployment of health HR has not been fully rationalized as
there is inadequate deployment in underserved, remote and tribal areas.
● Convergence issues with various implementation agencies like ICDS, education
department, water and sanitation and rural development. Lack of coordination among
frontline providers (ANM, AWW, ASHA) for delivering services towards common goal
of health.
● There is no clear cut policy and systems to provide free generic medicines in public
health facilities across States. Also, States lack adequate Institutional mechanism for
procurement, and supply chain management of drugs. Many States are lacking
rationalized Essential Drugs List (EDL) and published drug formulary.
● Delay in the registration and cash disbursement to beneficiaries under JSY .
● There may be inadequate coordination between the State Health Society and the State
Health Department. Also, insufficient tenure of Mission directors causes leadership
deficit.
Private
● NRHM continues to improve outreach mainly through strengthening of public sector
health facilities and the involvement of private sector is presently limited to a few areas
such as Blindness Control, RNTCP, family planning institutional deliveries and patient
transport. However, the presence of private sector in rural areas, particularly in remote
locations, is negligible.
Action Taken
● States have involved PRIs in the implementation of health and family welfare
programme through progressive transfer of funds clear articulation of functions and by
training equipping and empowering them suitably to manage and supervise the
functioning of health facilities.
● Technical support agencies like NHSRC and SHSRC have been created at National and
State levels to provide handholding support to the States to aid Decentralized planning.
● States are now required to report the progress of construction works as part of

for Grants to the Committee. No further proposers has been made in the projects
envisaged. (Para 3.22)
VI. CENTRAL INSTITUTE OF PSYCHIATRY (CIP), RANCHI
The Committee notes with concern that under utilisation of allocated funds has been
mainly due to delay in various projects. Further due to undue delay there has been cost
escalation also. Measures should be taken to check any further cost escalation due to delay
in execution of projects envisaged. (Para 3.27)
VIII. LADY HARDING MEDICAL COLLEGE
The Committee is constraint to note the continuous vacancies in all the grades and
the effects on the services provided and standard of education imparted. The Committee
regrets to note that the steps taken by the Ministry have not overcome shortage of
manpower at LHMC. The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Ministry to take all out
measures in filling all the vacancies in the period targeted and informed to the Committee.
(Para 3.30)
IX. ALL INDIA INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCE (AIIMS)
The Committee takes note that out of 23 projects only 10 have been completed, 3
have been abandoned. The Committee also notes that many projects are being delayed due
to non-clearance from statutory bodies. The Committee feels that this would result in cost
escalation and delay in providing services to the patients. The Committee, therefore,
recommends to the Ministry to take steps to ensure that pending issues on project
approvals, sanctions etc are sorted out urgently. (Para 3.34)
The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the progress made towards starting
Burns Unit at Jai Prakash Narayan Apex Trauma Center (JPNATC.) (Para 3.37)
XI. THE POST-GRADUATE INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH
(PGIMER), CHANDIGARH
The Committee would like the Department to take necessary step to overcome the
manpower shortage. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the progress in this
regard. (Para 3.40)
XII. NORTH EASTERN INDIRA GANDHI REGIONAL INSTITUTE OF HEALTH AND
MEDICAL SCIENCES (NEIGRIHMS), SHILLONG
The Committee in its various Reports on Demands for Grants has been impressing
upon the Department to ensure that all pre-project activities/approvals are completed/
obtained on time so that the projects are not plagued with delays for want of approval and
time and cost overruns are minimized. The Committee is however, constrained to note that
due to delay in approval, the proposed projects of NEIGRIHMS have led to upward revision
of costs of the projects. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should
widen its ambit of monitoring and ensure implementation of the projects at the earliest.
(Para 3.43)

90
The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the progress made in this regard.
(Para 3.46)
XIII. PRADHAN MANTRI SWASTHYA SURAKSHA YOJANA (PMSSY)
The Committee notes that the there is need for acceleration of rate of work in all
the projects and to devise strategies for successful running of these institution. Bottlenecks
at various stages of work should be removed with proper co-ordination among all the
concerned agencies. There must be effective monitoring of the status of the projects and the
monitoring agencies may be made accountable for day to day update on the projects.
(Para 3.49)
The Committee observes that the above projects are formulated and funded by the
Department. Therefore, the onus of completing them within the specified time-frame and
ensuring better financial performance lies with the Department. The Committee, therefore,
recommends to the Department to widen its monitoring ambit and ensure that the projects
under PMMSY are not plagued with time and cost overruns. (Para 3.52)
XIV. DEVELOPMENT OF NURSING SERVICES
The Department should fix a high standard for achievement and strictly adhere to
the time-frame and achieve targets. (Para 3.55)
The Committee notes that more needs to be done in this area than what is being
done at present to maintain a minimum standard in the private nursing institutions. A new
evaluation policy should be framed to balance the demand and quality. (Para 3.58)
XV. NATIONAL MENTAL HEALTH PROGRAMME
The Committee is dismayed to note that gross under-utilisation of allocated funds
has become a persistent trend under this head and that the Department has sought to shift
the onus on the State Governments for non-submission of utilisation certificates. The
Committee would like the Department to closely monitor the pace of implementation of the
schemes of NMHP at the State level for the sake of better financial performance under this
head. (Para 3.63)
The reply of the Department that the underutilisation of funds has primarily been
for the reason of fulfilling of unavoidable mandatory requirement of financial propriety, is
untenable and reflects poorly on the functioning of the Department. The Department should
focus more on devising ways of ensuring optimum utilisation of allocated funds than relying
on alibis for financial underperformance. (Para 3.66)
XVII. SERA AND V ACCINE MANUFACTURING UNITS
The reply of the Ministry is deafeningly silent about main recommendation of the
Committee, i.e., to formulate new strategies to attain optimum utilisation of funds and
revival of CRI, Kasauli and BCGVL, Guindy. The Committee reiterates its earlier
recommendation and desires that strategies be formulated to ensure optimum utilisation of
funds under this above head. The Committee desires to be apprised of the details of the
progress made towards making the sera and vaccine manufacturing units GMP compliant
and operational. (Para 3.70)

91
XVIII. ASSISTANCE FOR CAPACITY BUILDING .
The Committee notes that the issue is of utmost importance and must be taken up
on priority basis and work in this regard must be started as early as possible.  (Para 3.73)
XX. THE NATIONAL PROGRAMME FOR HEALTH CARE OF THE ELDERLY (NPHCE)
The Committee notes that the issues giving rise to under-utilization have not been
addressed and thus the Ministry should pursue the matter diligently. The Committee feels
that there is lack of proper planning for fund utilisation and targets are not properly
defined. The Department needs to work efficiently in this regard and take up with the
states. (Para 3.76)
XXI DISTRICT HOSPITALS
The Committee is constrained to observe that this is yet another example of causal
reply of the Ministry. No mention has been made regarding measures taken or contemplated
to be taken for holding frequent meetings with the States and impress upon them to submit
UCs on time. The Committee would therefore like the Ministry to take tangible action in
this regard and apprise the Committee accordingly. (Para 3.79)

92
(PART-B — NATIONAL HEALTH MISSION)
II. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
The Committee feels that mere agreement with its views would not suffice. The
Committee would like to be informed of the steps taken so far/contemplated to be taken
in the future to reduce the out-of-pocket payments made by households in time of health
distress. The specific role which the National Health Mission would play in reducing the
exorbitant out-of-pocket expenses, may also be indicated. (Para 3.3)
The Committee is concerned to note that adequate budgetary allocation for schemes
which have a vital bearing on Universal Health coverage, could not be allocated despite the
Ministry’s own admission that these programme were considered important and are
mentioned in the Twelfth Plan Document. The Committee is not aware of the reasons
adduced by Ministry of Finance/Planning Commission for not allocating the required funds
and would therefore like to be apprised of the reasons. The Committee also notes that by
now the RE must have been made. The Committee, therefore, desires to be updated
whether the enhanced allocations have been made under this head, and if not, what
alternate arrangements have been made by the Ministry to ensure that the activities
proposed under this head do not suffer due to paucity of funds. (Para 3.9)
The Committee lends its full support to the Ministry’s demand for higher resource
allocation for NHM and recommends that the Planning Commission may be apprised of the
Committee’s view in the matter. The Committee also recommends that the Department of
Health and Family Welfare needs to put its case more effectively before the Planning
Commission/Finance Ministry so as to ensure that more funds are released for NHM. The
Committee would like to be apprised of the Planning Commission’s response in the matter.
(Para 3.16)
III. NRHM-RCH FLEXIBLE POOL
The Committee would like the Ministry to indicate the steps being taken towards
allocation of adequate funds under the heads under reference and the outcome thereof.
(Para 3.19)
The Committee is constrained to note that the reply of the Ministry is evasive
inasmuch as it fails to indicate the targets set vis-à-vis achievements made, which was crux
of its recommendation. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation that the
targets set as well as the achievements made under NVBDCP may be indicated. The targets
set should be achieved, both physical and financial. (Para 3.22)
The Ministry should also have indicated the roadmap to put in place an effective
system of coordination with the States for timely liquidation of UCs.The Committee would
therefore, like to be apprised of the follow-up action taken by the Department with the
State Departments to ensure timely liquidation of pending UCs. (Para 3.25)
The Committee hopes that the Department’s new strategy to carry out house to
house survey to detect hidden leprosy cases and to treat them early would help in
eliminating spread of the disease. The Committee would like the Department to make an
92

93
assessment of the impact of the new strategy and intimate the Committee of the same.
(Para 3.28)
IX. MISSION FLEXIBLE POOL
The Committee recommends that 100% upgradation should be completed of the
earliest. There should not be any delay in this. (Para 3.32)
The Committee observes that it has not been informed of the final outcome of the
initiatives taken by the Department for their skill development and career progression. The
Committee would like to be apprised accordingly. (Para 3.35)
The Committee recommends the Department to fast-track its decision on revising
incentives for ASHA’s and make it commensurate with her job responsibilities.  (Para 3.38)
X. RCH FLEXIBLE POOL
The Committee desires that efforts should be continued to reduce MMR, IMR and
TFR. Monitoring mechanism should be strengthened. (Para 3.46)
The Committee notes from the reply furnished that three Committees have been
constituted to review the existing provisions of the Pre-conception (PC) and Pre-Natal
Diagnostic Techniques (PNDT) Act. The Committee would like to be apprised of the salient
recommendation made in this Report of the Committees and Action taken by the
Government on their findings. (Para 3.55)
XI. MILLENIUM DEVELOPMENT GOALS (MDGS)
The Committee while noting the efforts being taken by the Department to combat
malaria, feels that the Dengue and Chikungunya are emerging as new threats in the
country. The Committee feels that in addition to the efforts being made to control Dengue
and Chikungunya, efforts should be made by the Ministry to explore the possibility of
developing drug/vaccine for fighting these two mosquito borne diseases. Adequate funds
should be earmarked for development of ‘research’ on ‘Mosquito borne’ diseases.
(Para 3.62)
XII. IMPLEMENTATION OF NRHM (PHASE-I)
The Committee strongly observes that the Department should not get complacent by
releasing funds to the States and instead follow-up and constantly monitor the utilization of
funds. State Governments may be impressed upon the need to send proposals. (Para 3.67)
XIII. NEW SCHEMES DURING TWELFTH PLAN
The Committee recommend that the Department should move faster for
implementation of the said Scheme as the second year of the 12
th Plan is already in progress
and still the basic implementation framework of the scheme is being prepared and has not
been finalized so far. (Para 3.70)
